What is your opinion of Tito?

Josip "Tito" Broz has been one of the most fascinating politicians and nation leaders of the 20th century for me, and probably the only communist I can respect.

Rather than to get entangled with either the Bloc or the NATO, he went for third way independence and carefully played both factions against each other to get the best deal for his own people.

While he has been a communist, he was always very pragmatic und undogmatic about it and keeping roads wide open to the more prosperous free markets of the west, such as by getting industrial contracts with western corporations or allowing Yugoslavs to work abroad.

He has of course committed atrocities (read up on Goli Otok if you want to learn more about that), but ultimately he has brought the longest period of peace and prosperity to the region that it has ever known, and it would probably have been impossible to keep such a volatile country running without violently culling threats against its stability such as old Croatian fascist or Stalinist sympathizers.

His biggest fault was probably that he didn't take enough measures to keep Yugoslavia running after his death. The stability of Yugoslavia was heavily tied to his personal mixed heritage, war efforts against his own Croatian people and diplomatic skills to outmaneuver the more powerful countries. It survived his death for 10 more years, but the sudden collapse of the Bloc that until then made Yugoslavia very vulnerable to be eaten by the USSR in the case of a civil war led to the known results of war, atrocities and the weakening of the resulting divided splinter states.

I think he was probably in the middle in terms of talent in band. Brothers Michael and Jermaine were better, with Michael obviously having the most successful career outside of the band. Jackie and Marlon were clearly lesser talents.

Arguably the best of European Communist leaders. I don't view him warmly as all of the European Communist regimes had anti-Western foreign policies (hostility to apartheid, colonialism, etc) but he was kind of a 'liberal communist' in that the country was not intensely autocratic and had a decentralized, worker centered system somewhat akin to anarchism. A Serbian physicist friend of mine noted that he talked like a socialist and lived like a Rockefeller though.
